elements.content: Grammar focus: Future in the Past.

Anchor the story in the past, then choose the shade of future: would for neutral reporting, was going to for intention, was about to for the next moment, was to for a formal plan. In reported speech the future shifts back one step, which is why will becomes would.

would + base — neutral future from the past: he said he would call
was / were going to + base — intention, often unfulfilled: we were going to launch in March
was / were about to + base — immediate future, interrupted: she was about to sign
was / were to + base — formal arrangement or destiny: the board was to meet the next morning
was / were due to + base — scheduled future: the report was due to appear in June
past perfect of be going to — earlier intention in reported speech: he had been going to resign
Guided practice: choose the correct option.
1. Complete: 'They said the launch ___ in June.'
2. Complete: 'We ___ to publish in March, but the audit intervened.'
3. Complete: 'She was ___ to sign when the call came.'
Read and listen: three examples in context.

They would announce the result at noon. — Future from a past viewpoint. (Would + base.)
We were going to publish in March. — Intention, often unfulfilled. (Was going to + base.)
She was about to sign. — Immediate future, interrupted. (Was about to + base.)
What do you observe?

Future in the past reports a future that was still ahead when the story is set. Would plus the base verb is the neutral form in reported speech and narrative. Was going to marks an intention, and often implies that it was not carried out. Was about to marks the immediate future, usually interrupted. Was to marks an arrangement or a plan in formal narrative.
1. Which form often implies the plan did not happen?
2. What does was about to emphasise?
State the rule in one sentence, without looking at the table.
Freer production: I can talk about plans that changed.

Success criteria:
- I can report a past future with would.
- I can use was going to for an unfulfilled intention.
- I can use was about to for an interrupted moment.
Role play: put your position in ninety seconds; your partner notes every use of the target structure.
Frequent errors and correction:

❌ He said he will call on Friday (future not shifted in reported speech) → ✅ He said he would call on Friday
❌ She was about signing when the call came (missing to after about) → ✅ She was about to sign when the call came
Correct these sentences: say what is wrong, then give the right version.
Acceptable variants:

They said the review would start in May.
We were going to expand, but the funding was withdrawn.
He was about to speak when the chair closed the meeting.
Adapt the same task to the group:

- Individual: five sentences with the structure, on the topic of the lesson.
- Pair: a ten-line dialogue where future in the past carries the argument.
- Group: a six-minute debate, two sides, the structure required in every turn.
- Professional audience: transpose the structure into a memo.
- Academic audience: transpose it into a paragraph of analysis.
